title: Expert-review rubric + reviewer-handoff template (dual sign-off, COI, conflict resolution)
context: Dual expert sign-off (oncology clinician + patient advocate) is a hard blocking gate for every patient-facing QPL set. Without a shared rubric, reviewers apply different criteria, sign-offs lack evidentiary structure, and conflict resolution has no agreed procedure. A reviewer-handoff template ensures each reviewer receives the same package (draft set, agent UNCERTAIN: flags, provenance list, COI declaration form) and returns the same artifacts. This rubric is also needed to onboard and align reviewers recruited in qpl-reviewers-001.
objective: Write templates/review-rubric.md and templates/reviewer-handoff.md. The rubric defines the exact checklist each reviewer applies (clinician: clinical accuracy, no advice/prognosis, no leading framing, missing critical question; advocate: plain language, tone, sensitivity, cultural appropriateness, support resources); COI declaration requirements; and the conflict-resolution procedure. The handoff template is the package sent to each reviewer for a specific set.
acceptanceCriteria: templates/review-rubric.md contains distinct checklist sections for (a) clinician review and (b) patient-advocate review, each with specific, checkable items derived from the PLAN quality gates

The rubric specifies: COI declaration required from each reviewer; reviewer independence rule (drafter may not be sole reviewer); topic-appropriate reviewer requirement for sensitive sets (palliative for end-of-life, genetic counsellor for hereditary); conflict-resolution procedure ending with 'conservative reading wins'
The rubric states explicitly: no sign-off may be recorded while any UNCERTAIN: flag in the set's review.agentFlags is unresolved

templates/reviewer-handoff.md is a fill-in template that packages (set file path, agent flags list, provenance list, style guide reference, rubric reference, COI declaration block, sign-off block with date + reviewer name + credentials + COI statement)
At least one credentialed oncology clinician and one patient advocate have reviewed and approved the rubric and handoff template; sign-off recorded in the PR
Both files are concise enough for a reviewer to read in a single sitting (rubric under 1500 words; handoff template under 500 words)
resources: PLAN.md (Quality, review and risk gates section; Reviewer independence; Conflict resolution; Agent uncertainty self-check)
templates/style-guide.md (qpl-style-001 — rubric depends on style guide being finalized first)
